requirements.evidence: Most of the contract is present: EntityInvite model/factory/migration (app/Models/EntityInvite.php:11-82, database/factories/EntityInviteFactory.php:14-37, database/migrations/2026_10_29_000001_create_entity_invites_table.php:12-33), Entity::invites() (app/Models/Entity.php:41-44), queued mailable (app/Mail/EntityInviteMail.php:13,24-35), invite/cancel/role/removal actions (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:50-205), PendingInvites (app/Livewire/Entity/PendingInvites.php:23-82), switcher/onboarding/email/lang wiring. Deviations: an unrequested verified-e-mail gate (app/Livewire/Entity/PendingInvites.php:91,102) and two calls to UserRole::manageable() (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:59,176) that no file in the diff defines, so sendInvite()/saveRole() may fail at runtime.

conventions.evidence: Good: generated migration with reversible down() and a named unique index (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000001_create_entity_invites_table.php:12-33), deliberate #[Fillable] (app/Models/EntityInvite.php:11), scopes on the model, Blade components with {{ }} escaping, docs/CHANGELOG updated. Deviations: public input properties have no #[Validate]/rules() (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:34-40, validation only inline at :58-59 and :176), server-context state is not #[Locked] (Members.php:38,42), authorization uses inline abort_unless instead of a policy/gate (PendingInvites.php:102,107-109), and invite/membership writes live in the components instead of app/Actions/* (Members.php:93-103, PendingInvites.php:51-56).

security.evidence: Every mutating action authorizes server-side: sendInvite/cancelInvite/openMember/saveRole/confirmRemoval/removeMember (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:52,132,147,169,196,208), accept/decline re-check the e-mail against the invite (PendingInvites.php:28,75,107-109); user input inviteEmail/inviteRole/memberRole is validated (Members.php:58-59,176); IDs passed to actions are re-scoped through $this->entity (Members.php:249-251, render find). No {!! !!}, no secrets in public properties. Limited-impact gaps: selectedMembershipId/confirmingRemoval are unlocked (Members.php:38,42) and closeMember/cancelRemoval are unauthenticated state-only actions (:157,201).

tests.evidence: Broad Pest coverage: normalization/unique/cascade (tests/Feature/Entity/InvitesTest.php:15-42), pending e-mail matching (:45-54), accept/decline/expiry/idempotency/no-duplicate (:56-102), unauthorized accept/decline (:107-108), unverified 403 (:117), onboarding hr/locales and switcher (:132-158), mail in both locales (:160-183); MembersTest.php covers 403, invite happy path, validation, pending/expired, error-rendered-once, race, rate limit, cancel scoping, modal/role/removal flows (tests/Feature/Entity/MembersTest.php:28-293). Gap: no unauthorized-call tests for openMember/saveRole/confirmRemoval/removeMember, although conventions require one per action.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses model scopes (pending/forEmail) and small helpers (managerCount, selectedMembership, isUniqueViolation) instead of new layers; no speculative abstraction. Minor duplication: the same three-property reset is repeated in openMember/closeMember/removeMember (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:151-161,225-227) and ui.invites_pending_title duplicates ui.invites_title (lang/en/ui.php:103-104).

readability.evidence: Methods are short and named after their action, comments explain non-obvious rules (Members.php:62-67,80-82,178-179), style matches the sibling component, no debug output. Minor: isUniqueViolation() sniffs the exception text (Members.php:261-267) and members.blade.php is ~148 lines with two modals.

scope.evidence: The diff is almost entirely task material (model, factory, migration, mail, two components, four Blade views, lang, docs, tests); the Dashboard/layout edits are required to make members manager-only. Extras beyond the task: the verified-e-mail gate (PendingInvites.php:91,102), an unrequested self-removal session forget/redirect (Members.php:229-233) and an extra public closeMember action (:157).

issues.explanation: Both validation rules call UserRole::manageable(), which is not added anywhere in the diff (the previous code used a local ASSIGNABLE_ROLES constant); if the enum has no such method, sendInvite() and saveRole() throw BadMethodCallException and the two core actions cannot work.

The component silently hides invites and returns 403 for users whose e-mail is unverified, but the task says the invitee may accept on an e-mail match (only then 403) and that the list shows the signed-in user's pending invites, so this extra precondition can block the specified accept flow.

selectedMembershipId and confirmingRemoval are public, client-writable server-context state without #[Locked], contrary to the Livewire policy; impact is limited because membership IDs are always re-scoped through $this->entity before use.

The public input properties inviteEmail, inviteRole and memberRole carry no #[Validate] attribute or rules() method; rules are passed inline to $this->validate(), which still validates server-side but deviates from the project's stated Livewire pattern.
Authorization is done with inline abort_unless and custom protected helpers instead of a policy/gate invoked with $this->authorize(...), which the project conventions require for every action.

Invite creation, membership creation and invite deletion are domain writes performed directly in the Livewire components rather than in app/Actions/* classes as the conventions prescribe (though the existing Members component also wrote inline).
The self-removal session forget/redirect and the extra public closeMember() action are not requested by the task and add behavior beyond the specified removal flow.

There are no unauthorized-call tests for openMember(), saveRole(), confirmRemoval() or removeMember(), although the Livewire policy in conventions requires an unauthorized-call test for each action (only sendInvite/cancelInvite are covered).

firstOrCreate() keeps the existing membership row and role, so accepting an admin invite as a current employee leaves the employee role; the task says the membership is created with the invite role, even if keeping the old role is arguably safer.
isUniqueViolation() detects races by searching the exception message for "unique"/"duplicate" instead of checking SQLSTATE/errorInfo, which is fragile across database drivers and message locales.

The same selectedMembershipId/memberRole/confirmingRemoval reset block is duplicated in openMember(), closeMember() and removeMember() and could be one helper; lang key ui.invites_pending_title also duplicates ui.invites_title.

closeMember() and cancelRemoval() are public actions without any authorize() call; they only change local UI state, so the impact is negligible, but the Livewire policy asks for authorization on every public action.

review.summary: The change implements the invite-only membership flow end to end: model/factory/migration, queued themed mail, PendingInvites on the switcher and onboarding, manager-only members page with invite/pending lists, member detail modal, explicit save-role and removal confirmation, plus lang/docs/tests. The main reasons it is not approvable as is are the unrequested verified-e-mail gate that can block invitees and the UserRole::manageable() dependency that the diff never defines, together with several Livewire convention gaps (unlocked state, inline authorization, missing per-action unauthorized tests).
